**Annual Condition Inspection Form**
**Collection Stewardship Department**

**Inspection cycle:** 2025-01-05 through 2025-03-15
**Summary prepared by:** B. Hargrove, Collections Technician
**Date of summary:** 2025-03-15

This form summarizes the inspections completed during the winter cycle. Full individual
inspection sheets for each date are filed in the cabinet, binder 4. A total of 34 condition
checks were performed across the East Wing galleries, West Wing storage, and the study
collection. One exhibit change was made as a direct result of an inspection finding; all
other items were noted for monitoring or no action.

**Summary of follow-up actions taken since the start of the cycle:**

- **ENT-240, Cast iron skillet (Kitchen History Exhibit):** Light surface rust noted on
  the cooking surface during the 2025-01-14 inspection. I applied a light coat of food-safe
  mineral oil on 2025-01-16 per coordination with Dr. Vasquez. The skillet is back on the
  hanging rack. I will check it again at the next cycle.
- **West Wing basement storage room:** Dehumidifier hose was replaced by Facilities on
  2024-09-18; the room has remained dry through this cycle. I checked the room monthly
  (2025-01-12, 2025-02-09, 2025-03-08). No leaks or standing water observed. Floor is dry.
- **ENT-207, Framed print "Mill Pond" (East Wing, Room 2):** During the 2025-02-21
  inspection, I found the frame hanging slightly askew, about 1/4 inch lower on the right
  side. I straightened it on the same day. The hanging wire is intact; the picture hook is
  secure in the wall. No other action needed.

**Items noted for future action or continued monitoring:**

- **ENT-212, Walnut side chair (East Wing, Room 1):** The front left leg has a small
  wobble when weight is applied. This was noted in the 2024-09 inspection as well. The
  wobble has not increased. I recommend a glue-up at the next minor treatment session. No
  immediate risk.
- **ENT-218, Oil painting "Harbor Scene" (East Wing, Room 3):** The surface is slightly
  dull in the upper left corner. I suspect a light accumulation of grime. A conservator
  should evaluate during the next scheduled survey. No action taken this cycle.
- **ENT-225, Silver teapot (East Wing, Room 4):** I noted light tarnish on the lid and
  spout. This is expected for the display case with no climate control. I did not polish
  it, as polishing removes silver. I will flag for the exhibit team before the next
  rotation.
- **ENT-233, Quilt, "Log Cabin" pattern (study collection):** The quilt is in the flat
  storage drawer, file 14-C. I opened the drawer and checked the top fold. No new staining
  or insect activity. The drawer has a sachet of lavender that is losing scent; I will
  replace it at the next cycle.

**Condition checks completed this cycle (selected entries):**

---

**Condition check — Ceramic pitcher (ENT-235), West Wing storage, shelf C-3**

The pitcher is in its usual spot on shelf C-3, wrapped in its padded cover. I did not unwrap
it fully; I checked the visible rim and handle through the opening. No chips or cracks
observed. The cover is dusty but intact. No action needed.

---

**Condition check — Cast iron skillet (ENT-240), Kitchen History Exhibit**

The skillet is on the hanging rack above the reproduction stove. I noted light surface rust
on the cooking surface, which is a change from the 2024-03 inspection when the surface was
clean. The interior is not visible to visitors, so this is not an exhibit concern. I
recommend a light oil treatment before the next exhibit rotation. I will coordinate with
Dr. Vasquez.

---

**Condition check — Wooden butter mold (ENT-242), Kitchen History Exhibit**

The mold is in the wall case, bottom shelf, as stated. The carving is still sharp. I did not
see any new cracks. The case light is on a timer and was off during my inspection at 13:45.
No action needed.

**Condition check — Quilt, "Nine Patch" pattern (ENT-273), study collection**

The quilt is in the flat storage drawer, file 18-B. I opened the drawer and checked the top fold. No new staining or insect activity. The drawer has a sachet of lavender that is still fragrant; no replacement needed. No action needed.

---

**Condition check — Silver serving spoon set (ENT-276), East Wing, Room 4**

The set is in the display case, as stated. I noted light tarnish on the bowls of the spoons, which is a change from the 2024-03 inspection when the surface was bright. The tarnish is expected for the display case with no climate control. I did not polish the spoons, as polishing removes silver. I will flag for the exhibit team before the next rotation.

documents.content:
DESCRIPTION OF ISSUE
The glass display case GC-04-07 has developed a visible crack on the lower left corner of the front glass panel. The crack runs approximately 8–10 inches vertically from the bottom edge and appears to have a small chip at the starting point. No impact event has been reported by gallery staff or security. The case is currently locked and the interior environment is stable, but the crack is a safety hazard for visitors and staff, and it compromises the security seal of the case. The case contains six objects on loan from the St. Clair Collection (loan agreement L-2024-117); these objects are not currently at risk, but we request priority handling so the case can be repaired and the loan items remain undisturbed.

ADDITIONAL NOTES FROM REQUESTER
- The crack was first noticed by a gallery attendant during the morning walkthrough on 2025-04-01.
- The case was last inspected on 2025-03-15 as part of the monthly gallery check; no damage was noted at that time.
- Please coordinate with Collections staff before moving any objects; the loan agreement requires that a collections handler be present if the case is opened.
- The case has a climate monitoring sensor (ID: RH-204) mounted inside; please do not disconnect the sensor during repair. The sensor is currently reading temp 72F, RH 45%.

PRIORITY: HIGH
Justification: Public safety risk and security seal compromised. Case is in a high-traffic gallery with school group tours scheduled daily.

ASSIGNED STAFF
Name: Bob Hargrove (Maintenance II)
Phone: ext. 4477
Date Assigned: 2025-04-01
Time Assigned: 09:40

WORK ORDER STATUS: OPEN

Work Order WO-2025-014 work_order_type Repair work order type. Record status: current.

SCHEDULED WORK
Planned Start Date: 2025-04-02
Planned Completion Date: 2025-04-03 (tentative – subject to parts availability)

PARTS / MATERIALS NEEDED (per initial assessment)
- 1 x tempered glass panel, clear, 0.5 in thickness, dimensions to be confirmed by on-site measurement (case is custom-built, ca. 1998)
- 1 x glazing bead / trim kit (matching existing profile, bronze finish)
- 1 x silicone sealant (neutral cure, clear) – for re-sealing edges
- 4 x security screws (replacement, in case any are stripped during removal)
- 1 x lint-free cloth and glass cleaner (for final clean)

Note: Parts will be ordered after on-site measurement. Vendor: Acme Glass & Mirror (account #4451). Lead time for custom tempered glass is typically 5–7 business days.

SAFETY / ACCESS REQUIREMENTS
- Barricade area around case with stanchions and signage (per Facilities safety protocol).
- Do not open case without a Collections handler present (see note above).
- If the crack worsens during the barricade period, contact Security and Collections immediately.
- Gloves and safety glasses required when handling broken or cracked glass.

HISTORY / RELATED RECORDS
- Previous work on GC-04-07: WO-2024-088 (replaced interior light fixture, completed 2024-11-12).
- Previous work on Gallery 4: WO-2025-003 (adjusted door hinge on case GC-04-02, completed 2025-01-15). No relation to current issue.
- Monthly gallery inspection report for March 2025 (filed by J. Osei, Collections Assistant) notes no damage to GC-04-07 as of 2025-03-15.

COMMUNICATION LOG
- 2025-04-01 09:20 – R. Delgado paged B. Hargrove re: urgent repair.
- 2025-04-01 09:35 – B. Hargrove acknowledged assignment via radio.
- 2025-04-01 09:50 – B. Hargrove visited site, confirmed crack, took preliminary measurements. Left note for Collections: "Check back in fall re: seal integrity around the frame – old caulk looks dry."
- 2025-04-01 10:05 – Dr. Vasquez notified of barricade plan. She requested that a photo of the crack be taken for the loan file; photo taken by R. Delgado and attached to this work order.

documents.title: Work Order
documents.content:
CONTINUATION / FOLLOW-UP LOG (WO-2025-041)

2025-04-03 10:30 – B. Hargrove completed on-site measurement of GC-04-07. Dimensions for the
tempered glass panel confirmed: 48.25 in (W) x 30.5 in (H) x 0.5 in (thick). The existing
glazing bead is a bronze-finish, square-profile type, ca. 0.75 in wide. Sent measurement
and profile photo to Acme Glass & Mirror (account #4451). Requested quote and lead time
confirmation. Estimated delivery: 2025-04-10 to 2025-04-14.

2025-04-03 14:45 – R. Delgado (Facilities Admin) placed order with Acme Glass & Mirror.
PO #2025-0417. Confirmed price: $312.00 for glass panel, $48.00 for glazing bead kit,
$12.50 for sealant. Total with tax: $389.50. Order confirmation number: AGM-77812.
Expected ship date: 2025-04-09.

2025-04-04 09:15 – B. Hargrove checked barricade around GC-04-07. Stanchions and signage in
place. No change in crack. Noted that the crack appears to have a small chip at the lower
end – will monitor. Left note for Collections: "Crack stable, chip at bottom. Will check
daily."

2025-04-05 11:00 – J. Osei (Collections Assistant) emailed B. Hargrove re: the photo of the
crack taken on 2025-04-01. Requested that a second photo be taken with a ruler for scale,
for the loan file. B. Hargrove replied that he would take the photo on Monday (2025-04-07)
when he returns to the gallery.

2025-04-07 08:50 – B. Hargrove visited GC-04-07. Took photo with ruler per J. Osei's request.
Emailed photo to J. Osei and R. Delgado. Crack unchanged. Barricade intact. Checked seal
around frame – noted again that old caulk looks dry, but no active leak. Will address
during glass replacement.

2025-04-08 13:20 – R. Delgado checked order status with Acme Glass & Mirror. Glass panel
has been cut and is in tempering. Expected ship date confirmed: 2025-04-09. Delivery
likely 2025-04-10 or 2025-04-11.

2025-04-09 15:45 – B. Hargrove called Acme Glass & Mirror to confirm shipping. Glass panel
shipped via FedEx Ground. Tracking number: 7946 8821 3345. Estimated delivery:
2025-04-11 by end of day.

2025-04-10 10:00 – B. Hargrove performed a pre-installation walkthrough. Reviewed safety
protocol with R. Delgado. Confirmed that Collections handler J. Osei will be available
on 2025-04-11 at 09:00 to assist with opening the case. B. Hargrove noted that the
security screws on the case appear original and may be corroded – will have replacement
screws on hand.

2025-04-11 09:05 – B. Hargrove and J. Osei met at GC-04-07. Opened case. Removed cracked
glass panel. Inspected interior of case – no damage to contents. Removed old glazing
bead and cleaned frame channel. Noted that the old caulk was indeed dry and brittle, as
B. Hargrove had observed earlier. Removed all old sealant.

2025-04-11 09:40 – FedEx delivered glass panel to loading dock. B. Hargrove inspected
panel – no damage, dimensions correct. Proceeded with installation. Applied new glazing
bead, set glass, and sealed edges with clear silicone sealant. Replaced all four security
screws (two were stripped during removal, as anticipated). Final clean with lint-free
cloth and glass cleaner.

2025-04-11 10:20 – Installation complete. B. Hargrove inspected work – glass is secure,
seal is even, no visible defects. J. Osei inspected from inside the case – no issues.
Closed case and re-locked. Removed barricade. Notified Security that barricade was
removed.

2025-04-11 10:35 – R. Delgado updated work order status. Marked as COMPLETE. Noted that
final inspection by Dr. Vasquez is pending.

2025-04-11 14:00 – Dr. Vasquez visited Gallery 4 to inspect the repair. Confirmed that the
new glass panel is clear and properly installed. Noted that the seal around the frame
looks good. Approved work. Signed off on work order.
